candidates.exact_span: The current permit has a TRC limit of 0.019 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the prior enforceable TRC numeric limit; a different reading of which permit/version is 'current' could change the baseline limit used for FY2025 compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported TRC as being present in the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TRC was actually reported (vs. absent, below detection, or no-discharge) affects which measurements can be compared to limits (A), whether TRC monitoring was triggered (B), and how missing-or-present evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: However, the permittee uses potable water for filter backwash, which occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Discharge occurrence frequency and seasonality can change when effluent-related monitoring or limit comparisons are applicable versus periods treated as no-discharge or conditionally exempt.

candidates.exact_span: According to page 29 of the 2012 NMIP, which states that, "In instances where a facility uses chlorine for disinfection of the wastewater or is used as an emergency back-up to a system using another bacteria control technology such as ultraviolet light, or is used to remove filamentaceous algae, or when chlorine is used to disinfect process equipment used at the facility and the permit writer must limit TRC in the permit."
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting which chlorine-use circumstances trigger a mandatory TRC limit affects whether an enforceable numeric TRC limit is applicable at all and whether related monitoring obligations attach.

candidates.exact_span: Numeric criteria for Total Residual Chlorine are 19 micrograms per Liter (µg/L) at the point of discharge for Acute Aquatic Life designated uses and 11 ug/L for Wildlife Habitat and Chronic Aquatic Life Designated Uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable enforceable TRC numeric limit depends on which designated use(s) govern the receiving water; different use designations yield different limits (19 vs. 11 µg/L).

candidates.exact_span: At a stream critical low flow equal to zero (0), the limiting criteria is numeric criteria, which is 11 µg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The selected flow condition and rule for choosing numeric criteria determine whether the 11 µg/L limit applies instead of another criterion, changing the enforceable limit used in comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, TRC limit changed from 0.019 mg/L to 0.011 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Directly states the proposed enforceable TRC numeric limit; interpreting this as the operative FY2025 limit versus a rationale-only statement would change exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Monitoring requirements for the Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) are established in the proposed permit because the discharge enters the Colorado River Basin, in accordance with the current Salinity policy and program outlined in the most current "review, water quality standards for salinity, Colorado river system."
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TDS/salinity monitoring is imposed because of basin entry and salinity policy affects which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The objective of the policy is to achieve "no salt return" whenever practicable for industrial discharges and an incremental increase in salinity over the supply water for municipal dischargers.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifying the facility as industrial versus municipal changes which salinity objective and associated compliance framework apply, affecting both limit selection and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Under the Colorado Salinity Control Program (CSP), the facility is an existing facility where construction commenced on or before October 18, 1975.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Existing-facility status under CSP determines which regulatory tests and limits govern salt discharge; a different commencement-date interpretation could change applicable requirements.

candidates.exact_span: For existing industrial facilities, permitting authority may permit the salt discharge upon satisfactory demonstration that it meets one of three tests. The applicable test for the Aztec plant is that the existing tonnage of salt is less than one-ton (2000 lbs) per day or 366 tons per year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the operative salt-tonnage thresholds and the industrial-facility test pathway; different readings of facility type or which of the three tests applies would change limit/monitoring computations.

candidates.exact_span: TDS data obtained from the DMRs reveals that the discharge does not have a reasonable potential to exceed the 1 ton/day in salinity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reasonable-potential findings relieve or modify enforceable salt limits versus serving only as narrative support affects which numeric comparisons and monitoring tiers apply.

candidates.exact_span: The highest monthly average Total Dissolved Solids reported during the last two years is 19 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This reported concentration feeds salt-load and waiver determinations; treating it as the governing compliance value versus an illustrative maximum would change calculated loads and limit comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: TDS = 19 mg/l * 8.34 lbs/gal * 0.177 MGD * 1 ton / 2000 lbs = 0.0140 tons/day
candidates.computation_change_reason: The derived daily salt tonnage (0.0140 tons/day) is compared against the 1 ton/day threshold; different inputs, units, or flow assumptions in this calculation would change whether the facility is treated as under the limit.

candidates.exact_span: Since the TDS concentration is less than 500 mg/L, the discharge qualifies for a "fresh water waiver" irrespective of the total daily or annual or annual salt load.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A fresh-water waiver may remove or alter enforceable numeric limit comparisons and monitoring obligations; interpreting waiver scope (concentration-only vs. load-based) changes A/B outcomes and how no-result or waived periods are classified under C.

candidates.exact_span: Furthermore, the reported TDS is less than 1 ton/day, monitoring shall continue to be performed once every three months, using grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a continuing quarterly grab-sample monitoring obligation conditioned on reported load; different readings of whether this obligation is mandatory, report-only, or waived would change monitoring-applicability results and missing-evidence classification when results are absent.

candidates.exact_span: The dissolved Oxygen criteria according to 20.6.4.900.H (4) NMAC for warmwater, marginal warmwater and coolwater aquatic criteria are respectively 5 mg/L or more.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the numeric DO criterion (5 mg/L minimum) tied to aquatic-life use categories; which use class applies determines the enforceable limit for reported DO measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Since the facility is a water Treatment Plant, DO modeling is not required.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Exempting DO modeling affects which monitoring/modeling obligations are treated as required versus not required, and how absent modeling or DO results are classified when ordinary numeric results are missing.
